title: What qualifications does a person responsible for regulatory compliance (PRRC) need under the EU MDR?
description: What EU MDR Article 15 and MDCG 2019-7 require for the PRRC's qualifications, experience, duties and evidence, as at November 2026.
shortAnswer: Article 15 of the EU Medical Device Regulation (EU) 2017/745 requires every device manufacturer to have at least one person responsible for regulatory compliance (PRRC) with proven expertise: either a relevant degree or equivalent qualification plus at least one year of regulatory affairs or quality management experience with medical devices, or four years of such experience. Custom-made device makers may rely on two years of relevant manufacturing experience, and micro and small enterprises may use an external PRRC.
keyTakeaways: Route (a): a diploma or formal qualification in law, medicine, pharmacy, engineering or another relevant scientific discipline, plus at least one year of professional experience in medical device regulatory affairs or quality management systems. Route (b): four years of that experience.
The PRRC must be within the manufacturer's organization (an employee, per MDCG 2019-7 Rev.1), except for micro and small enterprises, which may contract an external PRRC.

The PRRC is responsible at least for conformity checks before release, technical documentation and the EU declaration of conformity, post-market surveillance, vigilance reporting, and investigational device statements.

MDCG 2019-7 Rev.1 (December 2023) says experience should relate to EU requirements and be substantive and recent; experience limited to administrative handling of documents or shadowing is not sufficient.

The PRRC's name and contact details are registered in EUDAMED, and MDCG 2019-7 says changes should be updated within one week. As at November 2026, Article 15 is unchanged in the latest consolidated MDR text.
jurisdiction: European Union (EU Member States; extended to the EEA and to Turkey under the Customs Union)
regulator: European Commission (Regulation (EU) 2017/745), Medical Device Coordination Group (MDCG) for guidance, and Member State competent authorities for market surveillance
appliesTo: Manufacturers placing medical devices, accessories or Annex XVI products on the EU market, whether established inside or outside the EU
Importers, distributors or others who assume manufacturer obligations under Article 16(1), and reprocessors under Article 17
In vitro diagnostic device manufacturers, under the parallel Article 15 of Regulation (EU) 2017/746 (IVDR)

sections.heading: What is a PRRC and who must appoint one?

blocks.text: The PRRC is a named, qualified individual who answers for a device manufacturer's core regulatory compliance tasks, and every manufacturer and authorized representative must have one. The role was introduced by [Article 15 of Regulation (EU) 2017/745 on medical devices (MDR)](https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legal-content/EN/TXT/HTML/?uri=CELEX:02017R0745-20261109), which has applied since 26 May 2021. The parallel provision in Article 15 of Regulation (EU) 2017/746 (IVDR) has applied since 26 May 2022.

The Medical Device Coordination Group's guidance [MDCG 2019-7 Rev.1](https://health.ec.europa.eu/document/download/463b4f08-44a2-4018-9957-488bf386fc3a_en?filename=md_mdcg_2019_7_guidance_art15_mdr_ivdr_en.pdf), published in December 2023, explains that the role is meant to ensure that supervision and control of manufacture, post-market surveillance and vigilance are carried out by someone who meets minimum qualification conditions. It applies to manufacturers inside or outside the EU placing devices on the Union market, and to authorized representatives of non-EU manufacturers. Where an importer, distributor or other party assumes manufacturer obligations under Article 16(1), or a reprocessor under Article 17, the PRRC obligation applies to them too.

Unlike most pages in this library, the PRRC rule is a qualification requirement rather than a training requirement: it fixes who may hold the role. Training still matters because the experience must be substantive, recent and tied to EU requirements. The requirements and guidance described are those applicable as at November 2026.

sections.heading: What qualifications and experience does the PRRC need?

blocks.text: The PRRC must show requisite expertise through one of two routes, or a third route for custom-made devices. Article 15(1) states the manufacturer's PRRC must have:

blocks.caption: PRRC qualification routes, MDR Article 15(1) and 15(6)
head: Route
Formal qualification
Professional experience required
rows: Diploma, certificate or other evidence of formal qualification on completion of a university degree, or a course of study recognized as equivalent by the Member State, in law, medicine, pharmacy, engineering or another relevant scientific discipline
At least one year in regulatory affairs or quality management systems relating to medical devices
Four years in regulatory affairs or quality management systems relating to medical devices
None required, without prejudice to national professional qualification rules
At least two years within a relevant field of manufacturing
Same as routes (a) or (b), with expertise in EU regulatory requirements for medical devices

blocks.text: MDCG 2019-7 adds detail. A qualification gained outside the EU is sufficient if one Member State has recognized it as equivalent. Experience "should be related to the EU requirements in the field" and should be "substantive, and recent". A footnote states that experience limited to administrative handling of documents and shadowing of regulatory affairs professionals would not be considered sufficient. For PRRCs of IVD manufacturers, appointees under route (a) should have relevant experience in the IVD field.

sections.heading: Must the PRRC be an employee, and where must they be located?

blocks.text: For most manufacturers, yes: the PRRC must be available "within their organisation", which MDCG 2019-7 reads as needing to be an employee. Each legal manufacturer within a group needs its own PRRC.

items: **Micro and small enterprises (Article 15(2)):** they need not have the PRRC within their organization but must have one "permanently and continuously at their disposal". MDCG 2019-7 allows a contract with an external organization, which should state the person's qualifications. This does not imply 24-hour availability but does require timely response. Per Commission Recommendation 2003/361/EC, a micro enterprise has fewer than 10 persons and turnover or balance sheet of no more than EUR 2 million; a small enterprise has fewer than 50 persons and no more than EUR 10 million.

**Location:** MDCG 2019-7 says the PRRC of an EU manufacturer should be located in the Union, and the PRRC of a non-EU manufacturer should be located outside the Union, ideally close to the manufacturing activities.

**Authorized representatives (Article 15(6)):** must have a PRRC permanently and continuously at their disposal, located in the Union. The authorized representative's PRRC cannot be the same person as the non-EU manufacturer's PRRC, even within the same group.
**Several PRRCs (Article 15(4)):** if responsibility is shared, each person's area must be stipulated in writing.

sections.heading: What is the PRRC responsible for?

blocks.text: The PRRC is responsible at least for five tasks listed in Article 15(3), and the manufacturer must give them the information and involvement needed to perform them.

blocks.title: MDR Article 15(3)
blocks.text: "The person responsible for regulatory compliance shall at least be responsible for ensuring that: (a) the conformity of the devices is appropriately checked, in accordance with the quality management system under which the devices are manufactured, before a device is released; (b) the technical documentation and the EU declaration of conformity are drawn up and kept up-to-date; (c) the post-market surveillance obligations are complied with in accordance with Article 10(10); (d) the reporting obligations referred to in Articles 87 to 91 are fulfilled; (e) in the case of investigational devices, the statement referred to in Section 4.1 of Chapter II of Annex XV is issued."

Article 15(5) protects the role: the PRRC "shall suffer no disadvantage" within the organization for properly fulfilling their duties, which MDCG 2019-7 says can include dismissal or being penalized. MDCG 2019-7 also expects the PRRC to tell the manufacturer if they cannot meet their obligations. The demonstration of device conformity remains the manufacturer's responsibility; the PRRC verifies it, for example by auditing or sampling release documentation.

sections.heading: What evidence of PRRC qualification should a manufacturer keep?

blocks.text: The manufacturer must gather sufficient evidence that the appointed PRRC meets the qualifications and can fulfill the role. MDCG 2019-7 gives examples: the curriculum vitae, copies of all relevant certificates, and evidence that the PRRC has actually obtained the required professional experience. It recommends recording and keeping these documents, which competent authorities may request during inspections under Article 93(3)(b) of the MDR.

Registration is also required. Annex VI, Part A, Section 1.4 requires the name, address and contact details of the PRRC to be submitted when manufacturers, authorized representatives and importers register in EUDAMED under Article 31. MDCG 2019-7 says changes, such as a new PRRC, should be updated within one week, in line with Article 31(4).

blocks.text: A structured [competency framework](/glossary/competency-framework) helps define what substantive regulatory experience means in practice, and [how to set up verification of competency](/guides/how-to-set-up-verification-of-competency) covers how to evidence it.

sections.heading: Has Article 15 changed since the MDR started to apply?

blocks.text: No. As at November 2026, the text of Article 15 in the EUR-Lex consolidated version of the MDR dated 9 November 2026 is the same as the original 2017 text. The MDR has been amended several times, including by Regulations (EU) 2020/561, 2023/607, 2024/1860 and 2025/2457, but none of those amendments changed the PRRC requirements.

The PRRC sits alongside the manufacturer's quality management system, which under Article 10(9) must address resource management, among other aspects. Training of other staff on MDR obligations is therefore a quality system matter rather than a PRRC qualification matter. For how quality management standards treat competence, see [ISO 9001 competence requirements](/regulations/iso-9001-competence-requirements).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry can represent the PRRC role as a set of defined competencies and responsibilities linked to the manufacturer's procedures for release, technical documentation, post-market surveillance and vigilance. That makes it easier to show which evidence supports the appointment and which procedures the PRRC verifies. See [healthcare and life sciences](/industries/healthcare-life-sciences).

faqs.q: Can one person be the PRRC for several companies?
faqs.a: For micro and small enterprises, an external PRRC may serve under contract, provided permanent and continuous availability is shown. For other manufacturers the PRRC must be within the organization, and MDCG 2019-7 says each legal manufacturer in a group needs its own PRRC. An authorized representative's PRRC cannot also be the non-EU manufacturer's PRRC.

faqs.q: Does a PRRC need a specific certification or course?
faqs.a: No. Article 15 sets qualification routes based on a degree or equivalent plus experience, or experience alone. No particular certificate is required. A course of study can count under route (a) only if a Member State recognizes it as equivalent to a university degree in a relevant discipline.

faqs.q: Does experience outside the EU count toward PRRC qualification?
faqs.a: It can, but MDCG 2019-7 says regulatory affairs or quality management experience should relate to EU requirements and be substantive and recent. A manufacturer relying on experience gained mainly under other regulatory systems should document how it covers EU device requirements.

faqs.q: Do IVD manufacturers need a separate PRRC?
faqs.a: IVD manufacturers need a PRRC under Article 15 of the IVDR, which mirrors the MDR provision with qualifications relating to in vitro diagnostic medical devices. MDCG 2019-7 notes that PRRCs appointed under route (a) for IVDs should have relevant experience in that field.
